facts.claim: In a review of 2976 studies, 99% of studies identified for inclusion had at least one area at high or unclear risk of bias or applicability concerns.
facts.quote: 99% of studies identified for inclusion had at least one area at high or unclear risk of bias or applicability concerns.

facts.claim: Extensive variation in methodology, terminology and outcome measures in deep learning studies can lead to an overestimation of the diagnostic accuracy of DL algorithms on medical imaging.
facts.quote: Heterogeneity was high between studies and extensive variation in methodology, terminology and outcome measures was noted. This can lead to an overestimation of the diagnostic accuracy of DL algorithms on medical imaging.

facts.claim: Deep learning models have diagnostic performance that is equivalent to that of health-care professionals.
facts.quote: Our review found the diagnostic performance of deep learning models to be equivalent to that of health-care professionals.

facts.claim: Radiologists were more specific than AI overall and in several subgroups, and were more sensitive to hip fractures before FDR correction.
facts.quote: Radiologists, on the other hand, were more specific than AI overall and in several subgroups, and more sensitive to hip fractures before FDR correction.

rejected.claim: In fracture detection on plain radiographs, clinicians and AI showed similar specificity, but AI leaned to higher sensitivity (7. 6%, p=0. 07).
rejected.quote: Clinicians and AI showed similar specificity in fracture identification, although AI leaned to higher sensitivity (7. 6%, p=0. 07).

rejected.claim: In a meta-research study of 423 systematic reviews, 57. 5% reported a high or unclear risk of bias in the patient selection domain.
rejected.quote: Two hundred forty-three of 423 studies (57. 5%) across all systematic reviews utilising QUADAS-2 reported a high or unclear risk of bias in the patient selection domain

research.angle: While deep learning systems can match or exceed human performance in specific diagnostic tasks, the evidence is undermined by high rates of bias, inconsistent reporting, and methodological variations.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that AI can perform as well as specialists in some areas, but the reliability of these claims is frequently compromised by poor study quality and lack of external validation.
research.caveat: A significant majority of studies identified in these reviews showed at least one area of high or unclear risk of bias or applicability concerns.
